slot.brief: Provide an aromatic ring with substituent(s) in a figure; ask major product of EAS directing the incoming group to correct position.

stem: The major product of the reaction shown in the figure is:

verdicts.working: The figure shows ethylbenzene but gives no reagent or reaction conditions. Ring bromination with Br₂/FeBr₃ can favor (C), while radical bromination conditions can give (D).
issues: The reaction reagent and conditions are missing, so the product cannot be uniquely determined.

verdicts.working: The figure shows only ethylbenzene; no reagents or conditions are given anywhere. With Br2/FeBr3 (electrophilic aromatic substitution), the ethyl group is o/p-directing and the major product is 1-bromo-4-ethylbenzene (C, para favored over ortho on steric grounds). With Br2/hv or NBS (radical conditions), benzylic bromination gives (1-bromoethyl)benzene (D). Meta (B) is not favored under either pathway. Since the reagent is missing, both C and D are defensible and no unique answer exists.
issues: Reagents/conditions are completely missing: the 'reaction shown in the figure' depicts only the starting material ethylbenzene with no arrow, reagent, or condition.

Without reagents the question is ambiguous: Br2/FeBr3 gives option C (para ring bromination) while Br2/hv or NBS gives option D (benzylic bromination), so more than one option is correct depending on assumed conditions.

working:
$-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ activates the ring and directs electrophilic substitution to ortho and para positions.
The para product is favoured over the ortho product due to lower steric hindrance.
Anhydrous $\text{FeBr}_3$ promotes ring bromination, not benzylic bromination.
Major product: 1-bromo-4-ethylbenzene.
